verdict.rationale: The official gitleaks-action runs Gitleaks on pull requests in GitHub workflows and uses a GitHub token to post review comments on PRs. That delivers the core of surfacing findings in PRs. However, the evidence is a few one-line claimed-docs mentions, GitHub only, with no hands-on corroboration. missing for 10: GitLab merge-request integration, documented check-run/annotation output, detail on what the PR comments contain, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can see scan findings surfaced as pull-request comments or checks in GitHub or GitLab

citations.quote: **gitleaks-action** uses this token to call [a GitHub API](https://octokit.github.io/rest.js/v18#pulls-create-review-comment) to comment on PRs.
Enable Gitleaks-Action in your GitHub workflows to be alerted when secrets are leaked as soon as they happen.
You can use it to automatically run a gitleaks scan on all your team's pull requests and commits
